title: Crew Sprintline: Deploy Journal, Staffing Roster & Release Notes (Apr 2026 draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operational journal for the April 2026 small-batch deploy (featureset v2026.04.2). Focus: staffing cadence, minute-level run notes for shift leads, and a release notes draft we can hand to PM/Comms after verification.

High-level summary:
- Release window: 2026-04-15 02:00 - 2026-04-15 12:00 PT (12hr window; primary cutover targeted at 03:30 PT).
- Scope: model routing update (route->variant mapping), small runtime kernel tweak (latency-sensitive path), and an opt-in cache warming job for high-traffic prefixes. No DB schema changes.
- Risk profile: medium (runtime kernel change affects hot path; guarded by canary and traffic shaping).
- Owner: Aisha Kapoor (release steward).

Goals for this deploy:
- Validate kernel tweak under production-like traffic without increasing p50 by >5% or p95 by >10%.
- Rollout model routing change to 20% traffic in canary, then 50% if stable, full rollout by end of window if telemetry green.
- Warm cache for top-20 prefixes to reduce early-threshold cold starts.

Staffing roster (primary + backups) - crew sprintline:
- Release steward (primary): Aisha Kapoor (pager -> DM on Slack C02ABCD1234).
- Platform/infra lead: Liam Chen (on-call/shift lead 02:00-08:00 PT). Backup: Rafael Gomez.
- Serving-runtime SME: Maya Singh (03:00-09:00 PT). Backup: T. Nguyen.
- Telemetry & SRE triage: Priya R. (02:00-10:00 PT). Backup: SRE rotation.
- Customer-support on watch: Noah B. (08:00-14:00 PT).
- Rollback gatekeeper (exec decision contact): Sarah M. (available 24/7 for this window).

Preflight checklist (to be completed by 2026-04-14 17:00 PT):
- [ ] Merge and CI green for platform PRs (PR #4821) - owner Liam.
- [ ] Smoke test run in staging with identical kernel flags (staging run id: staging-2026-04-10-7) - owner Maya.
- [ ] Canary configuration validated in test cluster: variant mapping, weights, and fallback policies - owner Aisha.
- [ ] Capacity runway check: verify GPU pool headroom >= 30% at peak ramp - owner Platform Infra.
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards pre-annotated: latency, error-rate, model-decoding-failures, KV cache hit-rate - owner Priya.
- [ ] Rollback artifact prepared: golden image tag v2026.04.1 and rollback playbook attached to incident board - owner Liam.
- [ ] Customer comms hold: draft release notes (below) saved to Confluence and CS notified of potential impact - owner PM (cc Noah).

Minute-by-minute deploy plan (concise):
- 02:00 PT: Ops channel open, all crew check-in. Run quick preflight checklist, confirm telemetry panels.
- 02:30 PT: Start cache-warming job (non-traffic affecting). Monitor cache hit-rate.
- 03:00 PT: Deploy kernel tweak to canary pool (5% traffic). Begin 30m observation window.
- 03:30 PT: If canary green, increase to 20% traffic. Continue observation 45m.
- 04:30 PT: If stable, bump to 50% traffic with staged ramping to avoid thundering. 1hr observation.
- 06:00 PT: Full rollout (subject to gate). If any throttle or regression at any step, stop and evaluate rollback criteria.

Canary & ramp rules (hard gates):
- Canary holds for each step until all of the following are true:
  - p50 latency delta <= +5% from baseline (last 7 days median).
  - p95 latency delta <= +10%.
  - Error rate (5m) not increased by >0.02 absolute or 50% relative, whichever is smaller.
  - KV cache hit-rate does not drop >5% during bump.
  - No new model-decoding-failures logged in last 10m.
- Manual approval required at 50%->100% (Sarah M. to sign-off) after a 60m stable window.

Telemetry & dashboards to monitor (links in Confluence):
- latency-overview (p50/p90/p95 per model and route)
- error-signal (5m and 1h rollups)
- model-failures and backoff-events
- infra-utilization: GPU utilization, queue-depth, host-memory
- KV cache hit-rate (per prefix top-100)
- user-facing SLA: percent requests within 300ms

Immediate rollback criteria (automatic/manual):
- Automatic rollback trigger: sustained p95 increase >20% for 10m OR error spike >0.5% absolute in 5m window.
- Manual rollback: any data integrity concern, cascading downstream dependency failures, or customer-impacting degradation flagged by CS/PM.
- Rollback steps (quick):
  1) Pause traffic reroute and point to v2026.04.1 golden image.
  2) Revert kernel flag via feature toggle (runtime control).
  3) Re-instate old routing mapping.
  4) Run smoke tests and confirm telemetry normal.
  5) Post incident retro and action items assigned.

Contingencies & fallbacks:
- If canary stability unclear after 2h at 50%: cut to 20% and open extended investigation channel (assign blamelist: infra, runtime, model).
- If GPU capacity shortage: enable reserved burst from Dedicated cluster (contracted capacity), inform CS of degraded throughput windows.
- If cache warming fails: revert warming job and rely on gradual ramp to let caches populate organically; monitor early latency spikes closely.

Release notes draft (to hand to PM/Comms after green):
Title: v2026.04.2 — model routing improvements and runtime latency optimizations
Summary: This release updates routing policies to better route specific request types to optimized model variants and includes a targeted runtime kernel optimization that reduces token-decoding latency for latency-sensitive workloads.
Notable user-facing changes:
- Smarter model routing: certain short-format and structured queries will be routed to low-latency variants, improving p50 latency for these flows by ~6–8% in internal tests.
- Backend latency optimizations: a hot-path kernel optimization to reduce decoding tail latency under typical request sizes.
- Cache warming: early rollout of prefix-based cache warming for top prefixes to reduce early-request cold starts.
Bug fixes / internal changes:
- Fixed a memory accounting edge-case that occasionally triggered ephemeral host OOMs in heavy burst tests.
- Small fix to logging format for function-calling breadcrumbs.
Known issues (we will call out if impacted):
- Some rare (0.001%) requests that use unusually long prompt chains may see slightly different decoding timing characteristics — no correctness impact expected.
- If the kernel tweak regresses in a non-obvious way, we may pause rollout and issue a targeted patch.

Post-deploy checklist (first 24h):
- [ ] Verify telemetry for 24h: latency, error-rate, cache-hit rates are within expected bounds - owner Priya.
- [ ] Capture perf snapshots for 3 representative routes and attach to PR.
- [ ] CS readiness: confirm no incoming high-priority tickets related to this change - owner Noah.
- [ ] Create retro notes and file ENGREL- follow-up tickets for actions.

Open questions / unresolved items (ACTIONABLE):
- Q1: Should we extend the kernel-opt to a second variant class before full rollout? (decision needed by 03:00 PT) — Action: Maya to advise with perf numbers from staging.
- Q2: Warming job concurrency level: current config uses 8 workers; do we reduce to 4 to avoid small early spikes? — Action: Platform to test lower concurrency on warm stage.
- Q3: If we see small increases in p50 but not p95, do we treat it as acceptable? Need explicit trade-off from PM. — Action: PM to confirm SLO flexibility.

After action / Postmortem template pointers:
- If rollback occurs, capture: timeline (minute granularity), telemetry snapshots before/after, last deploy logs (trace ids), and decision rationale. Use the postmortem template on Confluence (REL-crew-postmortem-template).

Appendix: quick command snippets for shift leads
- Pause routing (CLI): ./bin/route-control set-weight --route my-route --variant stable --weight 100
- Revert kernel flag (runtime toggle): curl -X POST https://ops-api.local/flags/kernel-opt -d '{"enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
- Smoke test command: ./scripts/smoke-run.sh --env prod --routes shortform --count 200

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc as the primary minute-level ledger during the window. I will append timeline notes directly under a new "timeline-journal" heading during the deploy.
- If anyone steps in to make a change, please prefix with initials and timestamp (e.g., "[A.K. 03:12] moved canary -> 20% (reason: baseline stable)").

End of draft.
